studies.Population: Singapore Chinese Health Study participants aged 45-74
studies.Reference: Low-carbohydrate diet score and risk of bladder cancer: Findings from a prospective cohort study.
studies.Authors: Pham YT, Wang R, Yuan JM, Luu HN
studies.comparison_type: per-SD increment in animal-based low-carbohydrate diet score
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: LCD scores were derived from the semi-quantitative food frequency questionnaire at baseline.

sample_size.excerpt: We used data from the Singapore Chinese Health Study, a prospective cohort study of 63 275 participants aged 45-74 living in Singapore who were recruited during 1993-1998 period.

cases.excerpt: After 17.6 years of follow-up with 819 573 person-years, 250 participants developed bladder cancer.

effect_size.excerpt: We found a statistically significant, positive association for bladder cancer risk with increasing level of animal-based LCD (HRper-SD increment = 1.16, 95% CI: 1.02-1.32; P trend = 0.01), but a null association with an increased level of plant-based LCD (HRper-SD increment = 1.08, 95% CI: 0.91-1.28, P trend = 0.78).

confidence_interval.excerpt: We found a statistically significant, positive association for bladder cancer risk with increasing level of animal-based LCD (HRper-SD increment = 1.16, 95% CI: 1.02-1.32; P trend = 0.01), but a null association with an increased level of plant-based LCD (HRper-SD increment = 1.08, 95% CI: 0.91-1.28, P trend = 0.78).

timing.excerpt: LCD scores were derived from the semi-quantitative food frequency questionnaire at baseline.
